shared_topics.title: Michigan Democratic Senate Primary: El-Sayed vs. Stevens — Aug. 5 Defining Moment
shared_topics.correlation_label: Same facts, sharply divergent stakes: left sees democratic energy, right sees electoral self-destruction
shared_topics.summary: Michigan Democrats head into their August 5 Senate primary with progressive insurgent Abdul El-Sayed polling roughly 15 points ahead of establishment candidate Haley Stevens. The outcome is broadly understood as a referendum on whether the Democratic Socialists of America wing or the party's moderate wing will define the party's identity heading into November. El-Sayed has energized younger and college-educated voters but trails the eventual Republican opponent by double digits in general-election polling.

left.framing: Left-leaning outlets frame the primary as a genuine and consequential democratic choice. Slate calls it the moment Democrats 'learn something critical about the party.' CNN covers it as a hard-fought contest with real policy stakes. The left generally avoids the electability question, emphasizing El-Sayed's coalition-building and his momentum.

right.framing: Right-leaning outlets frame El-Sayed's primary dominance as a trap Democrats are walking into. Breitbart headline-leads with the general-election number (El-Sayed trails the Republican by 10) rather than the primary lead. Townhall frames the DSA's 'politics of envy' as a liability in a general electorate. Fox spotlights the 'ogre on a pike' remark as evidence of radical rhetoric that will alienate swing voters.

shared_topics.title: Trump Takes Cabinet to Camp David as Iran War Pressure Mounts
shared_topics.correlation_label: Same events, divergent framing: left ties Iran to Trump's political fragility; right covers the military situation more independently
shared_topics.summary: President Trump convened a Cabinet retreat at Camp David on July 31 as the Iran war enters a precarious phase. The June ceasefire MOU has effectively collapsed, with both US and Iranian forces resuming strikes. Qatar and Pakistan are pushing a 10-day pause proposal, and the State Department issued fresh warnings to US citizens across the Middle East. The meeting also addressed the stalled Todd Blanche AG nomination.

left.framing: CNN and NBC frame Camp David as a retreat driven by domestic political pressure — Trump's approval at record lows, MAGA base frustrated, and a war without clear objectives. Coverage connects the Iran stall directly to broader Republican vulnerability ahead of midterms. The State Dept warning is treated as a sign of escalating danger, not resolved diplomacy.

right.framing: National Review covers the ceasefire collapse factually, noting that both US and Iranian forces resumed strikes after the MOU failed to hold. The American Conservative focuses on the conflict's spillover into UK politics — noting that Labour's refusal to join US-Israeli strikes has become politically agonizing in Britain. The right's framing is largely event-based rather than tied to Trump's domestic political standing.

gap_left.title: Trump Endorses Darline Graham for Lindsey Graham's South Carolina Senate Seat
gap_left.summary: President Trump has endorsed Darline Graham — a little-known candidate with no established political profile — for the special election to fill Lindsey Graham's former South Carolina Senate seat. South Carolina Republicans are described as baffled, with party insiders saying Trump 'threw us all a curveball.' The move is consistent with Trump's pattern of elevating loyalists over electability, but risks a competitive race in a state that had already rejected his first pick for governor.

gap_left.title: Abortion Rights Back on the Ballot in North Dakota and South Dakota
gap_left.summary: Abortion rights measures are heading to the ballot in North Dakota and South Dakota, where voters will weigh in on changes to the initiative threshold requirements that govern how abortion rights can be amended into state constitutions. Left-leaning outlets are covering the developments as part of the continuing post-Dobbs battleground, with NBC framing it as another front where Democrats see electoral opportunity in a state-by-state fight.

gap_left.title: Massie Joins House Democrats in War Powers Lawsuit Against White House Over Iran
gap_left.summary: Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) has joined House Democrats in an unprecedented lawsuit invoking the War Powers Act against the White House, challenging the legal basis for the ongoing Iran military campaign without a formal congressional authorization. Left-leaning outlets frame this as rare bipartisan constitutional pushback and a sign that the Iran war's legal footing is genuinely contested — even within the president's own party.

gap_right.title: Right Sounds Alarm on Mamdani's NYC Mayoralty: Muslim Brotherhood Links, Rising Violence
gap_right.summary: Conservative outlets are flagging what they describe as alarming ideological signals from newly-installed New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Fox News cites a report linking Mamdani's political network to Muslim Brotherhood-associated organizations, while The American Spectator frames his mayoralty as a preview of what socialist governance looks like when translated into actual policy. Right-leaning coverage treats Mamdani as a national warning sign, not merely a local political story.

gap_right.title: Wisconsin Democrat Cooke Reverses on Conversion Therapy Ban After Left-Wing Backlash
gap_right.summary: Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial candidate Rebecca Cooke reversed her position on a federal conversion therapy ban following pressure from the party's progressive wing. Fox News frames this as a case study in left-wing litmus tests forcing swing-district candidates into positions that alienate general-election voters, and as further evidence that Democratic candidates in competitive states face impossible choices between their base and the median voter.

gap_right.title: Indiana GOP House Speaker Steps Down After Blocking Trump's Redistricting Push
gap_right.summary: Indiana House Speaker Todd Bray resigned from his leadership position after leading the Republican state caucus in blocking President Trump's push to redraw congressional district lines before the midterms. The Daily Wire covers it as yet another instance of Republican elected officials resisting Trump's agenda — joining Cornyn and Tillis on the Blanche nomination as examples of intraparty friction that conservative media is cataloguing as a pattern of establishment betrayal.
